Getting started

Project initialization

kite init turns an existing Flutter application into a structured starting point with routing, theming, state foundations, shared feedback widgets, and managed generation metadata.

Run initialization

cd your_flutter_app
kite init

Preview without writing:

kite init --dry-run

Generated foundation

lib/ ├── app/ │ ├── app.dart │ ├── bootstrap.dart │ ├── router/ │ │ ├── app_router.dart │ │ ├── app_routes.dart │ │ └── generated_routes.dart │ └── theme/ │ ├── app_color_schemes.dart │ ├── app_theme.dart │ └── app_typography.dart ├── core/ │ ├── errors/ │ ├── result/ │ └── state/ ├── shared/widgets/ ├── features/ └── main.dart kite.yaml .kite/manifest.json

What each area owns

AreaResponsibility
app/Application bootstrap, Material 3 theme, navigation, and top-level composition.
core/Framework-level contracts and infrastructure shared across multiple features.
shared/Reusable presentation elements that are not owned by a single business feature.
features/Feature-first modules generated with Clean Architecture or MVC.
kite.yamlHuman-editable project generation preferences.
.kite/manifest.jsonKite-managed generation records, template versions, file paths, and checksums.

Initialization options

kite init --dry-run

Print the planned changes without modifying the project.

kite init --skip-existing

Preserve files that already exist and generate only missing targets.

kite init --force

Overwrite conflicts intentionally. Review the plan first.

kite init --no-dependencies

Generate source without running package dependency installation.

kite init --no-format

Skip formatting after generation.

kite init --path ./apps/mobile

Target a Flutter project outside the current directory.

!
Use force deliberately

--force is appropriate when you intentionally want Kite's current template to replace an existing file. It is not the default path for normal feature generation.
